note: Also measured against a victim domain that publishes NO DMARC record at all (DMARC absent, not p=none). The Local MTA spoof still works and is delivered to the Gmail INBOX. With no record, Rspamd cannot emit DMARC_POLICY_ALLOW; it emits DMARC_NA (+0.5) instead - but SPF and DKIM both pass (R_SPF_ALLOW -1 on the AlwaysData IP, R_DKIM_ALLOW -1 [alwaysdata.net:s=default], not aligned), so the net score stays negative and the message lands in the inbox. Scoring insight: an ABSENT DMARC record (DMARC_NA +0.5) is penalised LESS by Rspamd than an explicit p=none served through a third party in SPF (DMARC_POLICY_SOFTFAIL +1.5), so for Rspamd publishing nothing is 'cheaper' for the attacker than publishing p=none. On Gmail the message is delivered to the inbox (not spam): SPF PASS (AlwaysData IPv6 2a00:b6e0:1:a022::1), DKIM PASS (alwaysdata.net), DMARC FAIL (no alignment, no record) - Gmail does not spam a no-DMARC domain here. Gmail's exact long-term behaviour for no-DMARC senders is still being characterised.
